newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas dips amid western warming trend.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas dips amid western warming trend.

text.p: Canadian domestic spot natural gas prices were softer Tuesday as milder weather moved into Alberta, slowing storage withdrawals and spot purchases, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices fell more than 10 cents to about C$1.46-1.48 per gigajoule (GJ).
"It's on the back of all this warm weather," one Calgary-based trader said.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to reach a high of nine degrees Celsius today and 12 degrees C on Wednesday, sources said.
April AECO pricing hovered around C$1.39, while the April/October market was talked at C$1.42-1.43 per GJ.
At Sumas, prices inched up two cents to $1.27-1.30 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), as an unexpected outage kept supplies tight in British Columbia.
Westcoast Energy said 25 percent of production at its Pine River gas plant in northeastern B.C. would be cut Wednesday for about 16 hours so that operators can repair a leak on a boiler vapor line.
Total capacity at the plant is 340 million cubic feet per day.
At Niagara, prices for Wednesday delivery were mostly steady in the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s as cold weather in the East continued to keep buyers in the market.
